title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your makerspace assistant finishes a request and the program exits. The next morning, the same student starts a brand-new request. What is the only way the assistant can know what happened yesterday?

options.text: The model's own weights, changed by yesterday's conversation with the student
A note the program saved earlier and loads into the prompt
The context window, which keeps old text until it fills up
The final tool result, which the model still remembers from before

items.stem: A loop makes 4 model calls. The program re-sends the whole transcript each time, and the transcript grows by 500 tokens per step, so call n receives 500 x n tokens. How many input tokens are sent across all 4 calls?
Your search for "how do I clean the laser lens" returns a chunk that reads only "Remove it and wipe gently", with no machine named, and the model gets confused. Which change best fixes this?

options.text: A bigger context window so the chunk can hold more
Let the model guess which machine the chunk means
Add a header naming the machine and section to each chunk
Load every manual into the prompt so nothing is missed

items.stem: When the model decides to save a note to the memory store, who actually writes the file, the model or your program? Answer in one sentence and say why.
The assistant must keep cost low. Which one of these should it load at the start of every session, rather than retrieve on demand?

options.text: The full 90-page lathe manual, so nothing is ever missing
Every student's training note, so it can compare them
The whole year of booking history for all machines
This student's one-line training note, loaded at session start
